items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: when I went in with Lunceford's band, there was two of us went in there together. Saxophone player named Teddy Buckner from Detroit

ctx.x: Was it Teddy Buckner that plays now? trumpet near
Ted Buckner -- no, it was a saxophone player, Milt Buckner's brother. Milt Buckner, the piano and organ player used to play with Hamp. They were from Detroit. No relation to this Teddy Buckner.

items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: But we went in that band together. I never forgot that. It was September, '37.

ctx.x: Here. But he was a fine alto man. In fact, he was -- played the alto chorus on "Margie", the very first chorus. And Willie Smith always got credit for -- and Buckner used to feel so bad. He -- Willie got credit all the time for that chorus. And it wasn't Willy, it was Ted Buckner. And so, I guess -- that's the only alto they ever heard play solos with Lunceford prior to that time.

But we went in that band together. I never forgot that. It was September, '37. And we rehearsed about two, three weeks in New York before we ever went out on a job with that band. items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee narrates a story involving 'Rubberlegs' (Trummy Young) and Charlie Parker ('Byrd'), but does not explicitly state a personal relationship between himself and Rubberlegs, other than being present in the same anecdote.

ctx.x: If you get a chance, please try to hear it. I'll tell you a story on this particular date.

Rubberlegs was a big sissy, you know, great big guy, man, about 6'4"; he weighed about 240. And he loved Johnny Hodges, so he used to walk up to Johnny Hodges and -- let me feel it, man; he'd grab down there and grab that Johnny Hodges' penis, you know.

So Johnny, he say, I can't beat him. I just let him go feel it, he says, and then he go on. All right, he says, but you can't resist the guy, so big and strong. So he loved Johnny's playing, man. He just thought the world of -- anybody bother Johnny, he probably would have killed him.
